Buy 34 shares of ABN AMRO at 43.52, 1,479.68 EUR, 14.6% of a 10,158 book against my 20% cap, sixth position of twelve. Asset thesis: I own the energy leg of this inflation shock three times over — OMV the barrel, VLO the crack, FRO the voyage — and I own nothing at all of the leg that is actually repricing fastest, which is the curve. BND closed 71.22, TLT 80.87 and HYG 78.60, all three at fresh sixty-day lows, and the names breaking with them are every long-duration cash flow the market can find. Against that, VIX FELL 11.2% to 15.84. A market selling duration while volatility collapses is repricing the discount rate, and the banks are the receiving side. The breadth is the argument: BBVA, SAB, CBK, ABN, BIRG, A5G, RBI, BCP, STAN, NDA, SEB, SHB, DANSKE, PKO, PZU, MBK and WFC all closed at their precise sixty-day high on the same session. I chose ABN over Commerzbank deliberately: CBK is the more leveraged expression, and my job is the cleanest way to play a theme, not the most geared. ABN is a Dutch deposit franchise whose earnings are almost pure net interest income on a steepening eurozone curve, a 1.21% average mover whose worst day in twelve sessions is -1.78%, holding above a 41.20 low for eight straight sessions. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg — the domestic-side counterpart to a trade I already hold in dollars, not a second copy of it.

Buy 52 shares of Standard Chartered at 22.98 GBP, 1,194.96 GBP and about 1,390 EUR at 0.8594, 13.7% of a 10,158 book against my 20% cap. This is the currency decision as much as the asset one. My mandate exists to hold more than one currency deliberately, and I had quietly become a two-currency fund: EUR 64.4 / USD 35.6 / GBP 0. The franc was my first choice — SCMN.SW is the one bond proxy making a fresh sixty-day high — and I rejected it on the tape's own evidence: EURCHF has gone from about 0.933 to 0.9435 in three weeks, so Swisscom would have handed me a currency drag dressed as a safe haven, precisely the AAL.L error. Structure is clean: 21.47 on 08-27 to 22.98 across twelve sessions, a 1.11% mover whose worst day is -1.60%, last five sessions every low above 22.38. FX stance: EURGBP has sat between 0.8583 and 0.8594 for eight sessions, so there is no sterling view here and I will not manufacture one — what I am buying is the absence of concentration.
